subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 705 (Revised) - Material vs Pervasive Misstatements
question: Under SA 705 (Revised) 'Modifications to the Opinion in the Independent Auditor's Report', which opinion must the auditor express when financial statements are materially misstated AND the effects are PERVASIVE?
options: Adverse Opinion.
Qualified Opinion.
Disclaimer of Opinion.
Unmodified Opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph.
ref: SA 705 (Revised), Paragraph 8 - Adverse Opinion Criteria
explanation: Under SA 705 (Revised).8, the auditor shall express an Adverse Opinion when the auditor, having obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence, concludes that misstatements, individually or in the aggregate, are both material AND pervasive to the financial statements.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 705 (Revised) - Inability to Obtain SAAE (Disclaimer)
question: Due to seizure of all accounting servers and physical books by enforcement agencies, the auditor of Horizon Enterprises Ltd. is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence across all operational, revenue, and banking cycles. The possible effects of undetected misstatements are material and pervasive. What opinion must the auditor express?
options: Disclaimer of Opinion.
Qualified Opinion.
Adverse Opinion.
Clean Unmodified Opinion with a note in CARO.
ref: SA 705 (Revised), Paragraph 9 - Disclaimer of Opinion Criteria
explanation: Under SA 705 (Revised).9, the auditor shall disclaim an opinion when the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion (limitation on scope), and the auditor concludes that the possible effects on the financial statements of undetected misstatements, if any, could be both material and pervasive.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 701 - Key Audit Matters (KAM) vs Modified Opinion
question: Under SA 701 'Communicating Key Audit Matters in the Independent Auditor's Report', if a matter gives rise to a modified audit opinion (e.g. qualified or adverse opinion under SA 705), can that matter be reported in the Key Audit Matters section?
options: No. SA 701 explicitly prohibits communicating a matter giving rise to a modified opinion in the Key Audit Matters section; such matters are reported exclusively in the 'Basis for Modification' section, with a cross-reference in the KAM section.
Yes, all modified opinion matters must be duplicated word-for-word in the KAM section.
Only if approved by the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA).
Yes, because KAM is meant for negative findings only.
ref: SA 701, Paragraph 15 - Interaction Between KAM and Modified Opinions (SA 705)
explanation: Under SA 701.15, a matter giving rise to a modified opinion in accordance with SA 705 is by its nature a key audit matter. However, such matters shall not be described in the Key Audit Matters section; instead, the auditor shall report them in accordance with SA 705 in the Basis for Opinion section and include a reference in the KAM section pointing to the Basis for Modification section.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 706 (Revised) - Emphasis of Matter (EOM) Paragraph
question: Under SA 706 (Revised), what is the strict prerequisite before an auditor can include an Emphasis of Matter (EOM) paragraph in the auditor's report?
options: The matter must be fundamental to users' understanding of the financial statements AND must be appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements, and is not required to be modified under SA 705 or determined to be a KAM under SA 701.
The matter must be a secret fraud that management refused to disclose in the accounts.
The client must have achieved record profits during the year.
The auditor must be resigning from practice within 30 days.
ref: SA 706 (Revised), Paragraph 6 - Conditions for Including an Emphasis of Matter Paragraph
explanation: Under SA 706 (Revised).6, the auditor shall include an Emphasis of Matter paragraph provided: (a) The auditor would not be required to modify the opinion under SA 705 as a result of the matter; (b) The matter has not been determined to be a Key Audit Matter to be communicated in the auditor's report under SA 701; and (c) The matter is appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (i)(c) Title Deeds of Immovable Property
question: Under Clause (i)(c) of Paragraph 3 of CARO 2020, what is the auditor's reporting duty regarding title deeds of immovable properties?
options: Report whether the title deeds of all immovable properties (other than properties where the company is the lessee and lease agreements are duly executed) disclosed in financial statements are held in the name of the company; if not, provide specified tabular details including description, gross carrying value, held in whose name, relationship with promoter/director, and period held.
Verify only whether municipal property taxes were paid before March 31.
Auditors are only required to inspect property title deeds if requested by the local land registry.
Title deed verification is only required for agricultural land.
ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (i)(c) - Title Deeds of Immovable Property
explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (i)(c), the auditor must report whether the title deeds of all immovable properties (other than properties where the company is the lessee and lease agreements are executed) are held in the name of the company. If not, the auditor must provide details in a structured table specifying description, gross value, name of holder, relationship with promoters/directors, reason for not being held in company name, and dispute status.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (ii)(b) Quarterly Stock Statements vs Books
question: Under Clause (ii)(b) of CARO 2020, if a company has been sanctioned working capital limits in excess of ₹5 Crores from banks or financial institutions on the basis of security of current assets, what must the auditor report?
options: Whether quarterly returns or statements filed by the company with such banks or financial institutions are in agreement with the books of account of the company; if not, give details.
Whether the bank manager has visited the warehouse in each quarter.
Whether the company pays loan interest at repo rate or reverse repo rate.
Whether the company has mortgaged the residential flats of its directors.
ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (ii)(b) - Discrepancies in Working Capital Quarterly Filings
explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (ii)(b), whether during any point of time of the year, the company has been sanctioned working capital limits in excess of five crore rupees, in aggregate, from banks or financial institutions on the basis of security of current assets; whether the quarterly returns or statements filed by the company with such banks or financial institutions are in agreement with the books of account of the company of the respective quarters; and if not, give details.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (ix)(b) Wilful Defaulter Reporting
question: Under Clause (ix)(b) of CARO 2020, what must the statutory auditor report regarding wilful default?
options: Whether the company is a declared wilful defaulter by any bank or financial institution or other lender.
Whether any customer of the company has failed to pay an invoice within 30 days.
Whether directors of the company have defaulted on their personal credit cards.
Wilful default can only be reported under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (ix)(b) - Declared Wilful Defaulter
explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (ix)(b), the auditor is required to report whether the company is a declared wilful defaulter by any bank or financial institution or other lender in accordance with RBI guidelines.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (xi)(c) Whistle-Blower Complaints
question: Under Clause (xi)(c) of CARO 2020, what is the auditor's specific reporting requirement regarding whistle-blowers?
options: Whether the auditor has considered whistle-blower complaints, if any, received during the year by the company.
The auditor must disclose the identity and personal address of every whistle-blower.
The auditor must award monetary compensation to whistle-blowers from audit fees.
Whistle-blower complaints can only be considered by the Central Vigilance Commission.
ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (xi)(c) - Whistle-Blower Complaints Consideration
explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (xi)(c), the auditor must report whether the auditor has considered whistle-blower complaints, if any, received during the year by the company. The auditor evaluates complaints received via vigil mechanisms and assesses financial and fraud implications.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (xix) Financial Viability & Ratio Analysis
question: Under Clause (xix) of CARO 2020, what critical professional assessment must the auditor report regarding the company's financial viability?
options: On the basis of financial ratios, ageing and expected dates of realization of financial assets and payment of financial liabilities, other information accompanying the financial statements, and the auditor's knowledge of the Board and management plans, whether the auditor is of the opinion that no material uncertainty exists that the company is capable of meeting its liabilities existing at the date of balance sheet as and when they fall due within a period of one year from the balance sheet date.
Whether the company will make profits for the next 10 years guaranteed.
Whether the share price will double in the next fiscal year.
Clause (xix) only applies to Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs).
ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (xix) - Capability to Meet Liabilities Falling Due Within 1 Year
explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (xix), the auditor must evaluate financial ratios, ageing, realization timelines, and board plans to state whether the auditor is of the opinion that no material uncertainty exists as of the date of the audit report that the company is capable of meeting its liabilities existing at the date of balance sheet as and when they fall due within a period of one year from the balance sheet date.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 700 (Revised) - Ordering of Sections in Independent Auditor's Report
question: Under SA 700 (Revised) 'Forming an Opinion and Reporting on Financial Statements', what is the mandatory placement of the 'Opinion' and 'Basis for Opinion' sections in the independent auditor's report?
options: The 'Opinion' section shall be placed first, immediately followed by the 'Basis for Opinion' section.
The Opinion section must be placed at the very end of the report as an appendix.
Management Responsibilities must be placed first, followed by Auditor Responsibilities, and Opinion last.
The order of sections is left completely to the aesthetic discretion of the audit firm.
ref: SA 700 (Revised), Paragraphs 23, 24 & 28 - Structure of Independent Auditor's Report
explanation: Under SA 700 (Revised).23-28, the auditor's report shall have a clear title. The first section shall contain the auditor's opinion under the heading 'Opinion' (or 'Qualified Opinion', 'Adverse Opinion', 'Disclaimer of Opinion'). Immediately following the Opinion section, the report shall contain a section with the heading 'Basis for Opinion'.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 720 (Revised) - Auditor's Responsibilities Relating to Other Information
question: During statutory audit of a listed company, the auditor reviews the annual report and identifies a material inconsistency between the Chairman's Speech (stating export sales grew by 45%) and the audited financial statements (showing export sales fell by 12%). Management refuses to correct the Chairman's Speech. Under SA 720 (Revised), what must the auditor do?
options: Communicate the matter to TCWG; if not corrected prior to issuance, describe the material misstatement of the other information in the 'Other Information' section of the auditor's report.
Modify the audit opinion on the financial statements from unmodified to adverse.
File a police report against the Chairman.
Delete the Chairman's speech from the printed copies of the annual report.
ref: SA 720 (Revised), Paragraphs 16, 19 & 22 - Material Misstatement of the Other Information
explanation: Under SA 720 (Revised).16-22, if the auditor identifies a material misstatement of the other information that management refuses to correct, the auditor communicates with TCWG. If still uncorrected, the auditor describes the uncorrected material misstatement of the other information in the 'Other Information' section of the auditor's report. (The opinion on the financial statements is not modified because the financial statements themselves are correct).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (i)(d) Revaluation of PPE and Intangible Assets
question: Under Clause (i)(d) of CARO 2020, what is the reporting requirement if a company revalues its Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) or Right-of-Use assets or intangible assets?
options: Report whether the revaluation is based on the valuation by a Registered Valuer, and specify the amount of change if change is 10% or more in the aggregate of the net carrying value of each class of PPE or intangible assets.
Report whether the revaluation was approved by the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal.
Revaluation is strictly illegal under the Companies Act 2013 and requires criminal reporting.
Only revaluations exceeding ₹1,000 Crores need reporting.
ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (i)(d) - Revaluation by Registered Valuer
explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (i)(d), the auditor must report whether the company has revalued its Property, Plant and Equipment (including Right of Use assets) or intangible assets or both during the year and, if so, whether the revaluation is based on the valuation by a Registered Valuer; specify the amount of change, if change is 10% or more in the aggregate of the net carrying value of each class of Property, Plant and Equipment or intangible assets.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (viii) Unrecorded Income Disclosed in Tax Assessments
question: Under Clause (viii) of CARO 2020, what must the auditor report regarding undisclosed income?
options: Whether any transactions not recorded in the books of account have been surrendered or disclosed as income during the year in the tax assessments under the Income Tax Act, 1961 (such as search or survey or any other relevant provisions); and if so, whether the previously unrecorded income and related assets have been properly recorded in the books of account during the year.
Whether the company pays corporate tax at 22% or 25%.
Whether directors have paid their personal advance tax installments.
The auditor must report confidential search files directly to the press.
ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (viii) - Undisclosed Income Surrendered in Tax Assessments
explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (viii), the auditor must report whether any transactions not recorded in the books of account have been surrendered or disclosed as income during the year in the tax assessments under the Income Tax Act, 1961; and if so, whether the previously unrecorded income and related assets have been properly recorded in the books of account during the year.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 710 - Corresponding Figures vs Comparative Financial Statements
question: Under SA 710 'Comparative Information - Corresponding Figures and Comparative Financial Statements', which approach is adopted in India for reporting comparative financial statements under the Companies Act, 2013?
options: The 'Corresponding Figures' approach — where the auditor's opinion on the financial statements refers to the current period only, and does not refer to the corresponding figures unless prior period figures were modified, audited by predecessor auditor, or unaudited.
The 'Comparative Financial Statements' approach — where the auditor's opinion refers to each period for which financial statements are presented.
Comparative information is prohibited under Indian GAAP.
The auditor must issue two completely separate auditor's reports on different days.
ref: SA 710, Paragraphs 6, 10 & 13 - Corresponding Figures Approach in India
explanation: In India, financial statements are prepared using the 'Corresponding Figures' approach under SA 710. The auditor's opinion applies to the current period's financial statements as a whole. The auditor's opinion does not refer to corresponding figures unless the prior period audit report was modified, or the prior period financial statements were audited by another auditor (reported under Other Matter paragraph), or were unaudited.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (i)(e) Benami Property Proceedings
question: Under Clause (i)(e) of CARO 2020, what is the reporting obligation regarding Benami Transactions?
options: Whether any proceedings have been initiated or are pending against the company for holding any benami property under the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988 and rules made thereunder; if so, whether the company has appropriately disclosed the details in its financial statements.
Whether any shareholder has a nickname.
The auditor must conduct sting operations to seize benami properties.
Clause (i)(e) only applies if the benami property is worth over ₹100 Crores.
ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (i)(e) - Benami Transactions Reporting
explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (i)(e), the auditor must report whether any proceedings have been initiated or are pending against the company for holding any benami property under the Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988 (as amended in 2016) and rules made thereunder; and if so, whether the company has appropriately disclosed the details in its financial statements.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (xvii) Cash Losses Reporting
question: Under Clause (xvii) of CARO 2020, what must the auditor report regarding cash losses?
options: Whether the company has incurred cash losses in the financial year and in the immediately preceding financial year, and if so, state the amount of cash losses.
Whether petty cash was stolen from the cashier's drawer.
Whether the company pays cash salaries to daily wage laborers.
Cash losses are only reported if the company has defaulted on bank loans.
ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (xvii) - Reporting of Cash Losses
explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (xvii), the auditor must report whether the company has incurred cash losses in the financial year and in the immediately preceding financial year, and if so, state the amount of cash losses. (Cash loss = Net Profit/Loss after tax adjusted for non-cash items like depreciation, amortization, and deferred tax).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (xx) Unspent CSR Amounts
question: Under Clause (xx) of CARO 2020, what must the auditor report regarding Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) compliance under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Whether in respect of other than ongoing projects, the company has transferred unspent amount to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within 6 months of expiry of the financial year; and whether in respect of ongoing projects, unspent amount has been transferred to a special account (Unspent CSR Account) within 30 days of the end of the financial year.
Whether the CSR committee members attended all charity galas.
Whether the company planted at least 1,000 trees on World Environment Day.
CSR compliance reporting is voluntary and excluded from CARO 2020.
ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (xx) - CSR Unspent Amounts Transfer
explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (xx), the auditor reports compliance with Section 135(5) & 135(6): (a) For non-ongoing projects, unspent CSR funds must be transferred to a Schedule VII fund within 6 months of fiscal year-end; (b) For ongoing projects, unspent amounts must be transferred to a designated 'Unspent CSR Account' in a scheduled bank within 30 days of fiscal year-end.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 705 - Format of Modified Opinion Heading
question: When the auditor modifies the opinion under SA 705, how should the headings of the 'Opinion' and 'Basis for Opinion' sections be titled?
options: The headings must specifically state 'Qualified Opinion', 'Adverse Opinion', or 'Disclaimer of Opinion', and the basis section must be titled 'Basis for Qualified Opinion', 'Basis for Adverse Opinion', or 'Basis for Disclaimer of Opinion'.
They must retain the generic title 'Opinion' and 'Basis for Opinion' so readers are not alarmed.
The headings must be titled 'Statutory Legal Warning'.
Headings are deleted and replaced by an asterisks footnote.
ref: SA 705 (Revised), Paragraphs 16 & 20 - Specific Headings for Modified Opinions
explanation: Under SA 705 (Revised).16 & 20, when the auditor modifies the audit opinion, the auditor shall use the heading 'Qualified Opinion', 'Adverse Opinion', or 'Disclaimer of Opinion', as appropriate, for the Opinion section, and shall use the heading 'Basis for Qualified Opinion', 'Basis for Adverse Opinion', or 'Basis for Disclaimer of Opinion', as appropriate, for the Basis section.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (xxi) Qualifications in Group CFS
question: Under Clause (xxi) of CARO 2020, what is the group auditor's specific reporting responsibility in the CARO report on Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS)?
options: Report whether there have been any qualifications or adverse remarks by the respective auditors in the CARO reports of the companies included in the consolidated financial statements; if yes, indicate the details of the companies and paragraph numbers of the respective CARO reports.
Clause (xxi) exempts CFS from all CARO reporting.
The group auditor must rewrite the CARO report of all subsidiaries from scratch.
The auditor must only report if the parent company itself has a qualification.
ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (xxi) - Qualifications or Adverse Remarks in Group Components
explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (xxi), in the CARO report accompanying the consolidated financial statements, the auditor must report whether there have been any qualifications or adverse remarks by the respective auditors in the CARO reports of the companies included in the consolidated financial statements; if yes, specify the component names and the paragraph numbers containing such remarks.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 230 - Assembly of Final Audit File (60 Days Rule)
question: Under SA 230 and SQC 1, what is the mandatory regulatory timeline for the engagement team to assemble the final audit file after the date of the auditor's report?
options: Ordinarily not more than 60 days after the date of the auditor's report.
Within 180 days after the Annual General Meeting.
Before 5:00 PM on the day the audit report is signed.
Assembly can occur at any time within 7 years.
ref: SQC 1, Paragraph 75 & SA 230, Paragraph A21 - Assembly of Final Audit File
explanation: Under SQC 1.75 and SA 230.A21, the assembly of the final audit file after the date of the auditor's report is an administrative process that does not involve the performance of new audit procedures or the drawing of new conclusions. An appropriate time limit within which to complete the assembly of the final audit file is ordinarily not more than 60 days after the date of the auditor's report.
